questions.q: At what time in the flight does Starship hit Max-Q, and what is Max-Q?
questions.do: Look at the Flight sequence list and click Max-Q to jump there and read its description.
questions.a: At T+01:13. Max-Q is maximum dynamic pressure: speed and air density together give the biggest aerodynamic load of the climb.

questions.q: What is the heaviest payload that still gets the ship into orbit?
questions.do: In Mission setup, move the Payload slider up in 5 t steps and read the Flight computer line each time.
questions.a: 95 t. At 95 t the ship still reaches orbit with almost no propellant to spare. At 100 t the flight computer says it falls short of orbit by about 106 km/h.

questions.q: What happens to the launch if 3 of the 33 booster engines fail at liftoff?
questions.do: Set Engines out at liftoff to 3 of 33 (keep everything else at the start values) and read the Flight computer line.
questions.a: Liftoff thrust-to-weight drops from 1.28 to 1.17 and staging comes later, at T+02:47 instead of T+02:32. The ship still reaches orbit, with 2.4% of its propellant to spare. Fewer engines means less push for the same weight.

questions.q: Why does keeping more fuel in the booster for the trip home take speed away from the ship?
questions.do: Set Booster return reserve to 200 t and read the Flight computer line. Then set it to 400 t and read it again.
questions.a: With 200 t the booster cannot get home and ditches about 200 km offshore. With 400 t it is caught, but staging comes earlier (T+02:28, about 5,729 km/h) and the ship has only 2.4% to spare instead of 3.0%. Fuel saved for the return is fuel not used to push the ship upward.

questions.q: In this flight the hot-stage ring is thrown away after separation. What does the page say about later boosters?
questions.do: In the Flight sequence, click Hot-stage ring jettison (T+03:17) and read the description.
questions.a: The vented ring protected the booster dome during hot staging, and it is dropped to save mass for the landing. The page says later booster designs build it in, so the design changed as Starship developed.
